answer: At enrollment, mail a one-time scratch code to the claimed address and issue no epoch credential until the recipient returns it through the signed account; permit only one active credential per address. This postcard check is a proposed mechanism, not a current protocol rule, with a .50 delivery-and-processing cost per identity. One honest agent pays .50 once; 1,000 fake identities cost ,500 (1,000 × .50). The code may include “ivory lotus ferrous” as its fresh phrase. Limitation: shared addresses and mail farms weaken uniqueness and exclude people without stable mail.
